title: Same Old Narrative Driving Additional Gains
summary:
Same Old Narrative Driving Additional Gains 

             
             
            Stocks slid overnight and bond yields followed. This is the prevailing correlation as bonds serve as a safer haven for the money bleeding out of the previously bloated AI trade. It's not always 1:1 and today, that worked in our favor as bonds didn't give back nearly as much of intraday move as stocks (i.e. stocks erased most of the their losses by 2:30pm, but bonds  retained most of their gains). Such discrepancies could easily be explained by the excess, random volatility often associated with Thanksgiving trading considerations. We'll choose to be thankful that this is the way it played out this time around and we'll look forward to more liquid price discovery next week.

title: Mortgage Rates Improve Again as Stock Slide Continues
summary: As we discussed in greater detail yesterday, there's not a reliable rule for how stocks and interest rates correlate, but lately, lower stock prices have helped facilitate lower rates.  That phenomenon proved out this morning as overnight stock losses helped the bond market open in much stronger territory (and stronger bonds = lower rates).   Stocks ended up bouncing fairly decently in the early afternoon, but rates were less inclined to follow. We're not reading much into the weaker afternoon correlation simply due to the fact that the day before Thanksgiving often sees random volatility driven by a rush for the exits among traders.  By remaining in stronger territory, the bond market allowed mortgage lenders to set rates at another 2-week low with the top-tier 30yr fixed rate now down to 7.26% from 7.32% yesterday.   [thirtyyearmortgagerates]

title: AI Broker Mining, Investor AUS, HELOC Tools; New Conforming Loan Limits; Capital Markets
summary: In Northern California, the flooding and tides are real, impacting travel and potentially having longer-term ramifications for lenders and servicers. It’s that time of year when rate locks generally drop, and Freddie and Fannie traditionally set their conforming loan amounts for the subsequent year ($855,400, a 2.72 percent increase over the 2026 limit). Some of the thrill and anticipation of that has worn off, given the increase in non-Agency volumes helped by the lack of gfees and many loan level price adjustments that the FHFA insist on. Speaking of which, “Rob, you wrote that Bill Pulte stated his mission is to end fraud at Freddie and Fannie. But in September, Pulte’s FHFA slashed the budget of the independent office tasked with investigating fraud at Fannie and Freddie. The 2027 fiscal budget cut the FHFA’s Office of Inspector General’s funding by about 61 percent from the previous year. Who’s correct?” Actions speak louder than words? “The OIG said it is preparing to reduce 80 percent of its staff. The office’s national criminal enforcement program, as well as its participation in ongoing criminal cases with the Department of Justice and more than 30 U.S. Attorneys’ Offices will end.” (Today’s podcast can be found here. This week’s ‘casts are presented by Cenlar, which provides the highest level of mortgage servicing to client partners through the talent of its employees and extensive history of working with a diverse portfolio of banks, mortgage bankers, and credit unions. Today’s has an interview with VIUbyHUB’s Travis Hodges on embedding insurance into the mortgage experience and how lenders can evaluate these partnerships.)

title: Stunningly Small Reaction to Strong Econ Data
summary: GDP, core durable goods, and jobless claims all came in much stronger than expected. PCE inflation was right on target and supercore was actually lower. Despite all that, bonds did absolutely nothing at 8:30am and even managed to improve since then. The trading is completely disconnected from the data for a few reasons. First, these reports are not top-tier market movers. PCE is the most important for bonds, but largely already known based on the CPI/PPI data that came out 2 weeks ago. Second, the bond market is more interested in forward looking indicators like the stock market swoon (stocks aren't always an economic indicator, but they are right now). Third, it's the day before thanksgiving and market movement can be less logical than during more liquid/active times of year.  That implied volatility risk will increase throughout the day as traders leave early, but as always, it can play out in either direction.
